statusText: Green - all 24 published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, holding Tail at its structural floor
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains far below the block threshold and no evidence-based danger window applies, because every one of the 24 published hours falls inside the CME weekend halt and no NQ price path can form in any of them. The 22:00Z Sunday futures reopen lies roughly seven hours beyond the final slot in this window. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always.
headline: A halted weekend tape carries a just-hiked Fed, a 5% 10-year and ~$100 crude into an unpriced Sunday reopen, with Tail pinned at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini settled near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, roughly seven hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this assessment: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.6 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.998%, up 5.1bp, after trading back above 5.00% intraday, while the 2-year reached 4.75%, its highest since June 2024, against the 4.67% carried on the September 17 H.15. WTI traded near $100 and Brent near $102-104 after a third consecutive decline. The backdrop is genuinely tense. The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on September 16 by unanimous 12-0 vote, stating that inflation remains elevated and that the action supports a timelier return to the 2 percent goal. A drone attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline, the route built to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, has left Riyadh signalling half capacity within days and a full repair in roughly six weeks, with barrels rerouted through slower ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar in Oman. Reported U.S.-Gulf talks on Iran at the UN General Assembly sidelines remain an open checkpoint for the coming week. None of that changes the Tail assessment for this window. Tail measures a price path that denies mean reversion, and a halted market has no mechanism to produce one. Friday's session was rotational rather than one-way: semiconductors led sharply, with Lam Research up 6.98%, Seagate up 6.93% and Applied Materials up 6.51%, while Qualcomm fell 5.67% and IBM 3.45%, and NYSE decliners outnumbered advancers 1,794 to 919 beneath a higher index. It was also triple witching, so those closing marks carry expiry-flow distortion and are a weaker guide to underlying structure than a normal settle. Volatility finished at the low of its range. Tail therefore holds 5, eases to 4 through the deepest stretch of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches 6 from 10:00Z as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates ahead of a reopen that lies outside this window. Stress drifts from 23 to 30, crossing into the moderate band at 20:00Z Saturday on elapsed unpriced time rather than on any new stress event, and Confidence steps from 75 to 65 as verified Friday evidence ages with nothing able to refresh it.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 16-18 through Friday's dispersed, triple-witching cash session, then fell through 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final sixteen slots. Stress peaked at 50 in the Friday afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for six consecutive hours before settling at 22. Confidence held between 75 and 88, easing steadily once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode was mixed across the cash session, turned trend-up into the close and has read normal for every hour since the weekend halt began.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, roughly seven hours after the final slot here. Tail holds 5 for three hours, eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches 6 from 10:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Those steps reflect proximity and unpriced elapsed time, never observed structure. Stress drifts from 23 to 30, crossing into the moderate band at 20:00Z Saturday on staleness alone, and Confidence steps from 75 to 65 as Friday's verified evidence ages. Energy and Middle East headlines remain the most plausible weekend surprise vector, with the Saudi pipeline repair timeline and the reported U.S.-Gulf Iran talks at the UNGA sidelines the named checkpoints; any such development would raise Stress and reopen-gap risk first, and would reach Tail only if a reopened tape genuinely refused retracement. The first scheduled macro test is Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs, well beyond this window.
